newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - Swiss Nat Bank cuts discount rate to 1.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Swiss Nat Bank cuts discount rate to 1.0 pct.

text.p: Swiss National Bank (SNB) governors on Thursday to cut the discount rate by 50 basis points (0.5 percentage point) to 1.0 percent, matching a record low and weakening the strong Swiss franc.
A central bank statement said the move, effective Friday, September 27, was in line with the recent decline in Swiss money market rates.
An SNB spokesman said the bank decided to cut the discount rate as a means of underscoring the recent decline in money market rates.
"The (rate cut) move is more a reassurance to the market that the interest rate decline since August will not be reversed," SNB spokesman Werner Abegg said.
Market analysts said the move confirmed a trend already evident in the money market, and underscored the SNB's intentions to keep money rates low.
Money market traders had earlier said no cut was expected today, but added it could not be ruled out near-term.

The SNB pointed out in its statement that it had been supplying the money market with additional liquidity since the beginning of August "in order to prevent monetary strain" and as a result, some money market rates fell below the discount rate.
"By lowering the discount rate, the Swiss National Bank underlines its expectation that the interest rate decline will continue for some time," it added.

The discount rate was last cut to one percent in February 1978, a record low where it stayed until a return to 2.0 percent in November 1979. The most recent rate change was a drop of 50 basis points last December 14.
The Swiss franc, whose strength has been blamed in part for a sluggish economy by making exports expensive, fell against the dollar and German mark immediately after the SNB announcement.
The dollar rose to 1.2505/2515 Swiss francs about an hour after the SNB announcement from 1.2425 before the news.
CS Trading Research director Gerard Piasko said he expected both the dollar and mark to consolidate at higher levels against the Swisss franc in the short-term and seek further gains.
Piasko forecast a near-term mark/Swiss level around 82.35 and dollar above the 1.2500 mark.
Manfred Gutmann, senior economist at UBS, said the cut was not unexpected because short-term market rates had declined and the discount rate should be lower than those.
"This is a signal that they will continue their relatively strong supply of money...The signal is they want the Swiss franc exchange rate lower," Gutmann said.
Guttman said he expected no significant boost to the real economy, which has posted six quarters of declining gross domestic product (GDP).

He said UBS was sticking to a forecast that the franc would weaken slightly over the next three to six months, with short-term market rates below two percent, bonds at around four percent, and GDP growing 0.8 percent in 1997 after contracting 0.6 percent this year.
Swiss franc short rates fell sharply after the SNB announcement, while bond prices moved higher but to a lesser degree. Swiss shares mostly shrugged off the rate cut.
